geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the small notch-like subtraction with a true void-carving operation to strengthen the public court logic at the access edge.
Increase void depth/size so the subtraction reads as usable ground space.
Open the carved void toward the program-defined access side.
Wrap the mass with a split-wing logic to create a clearer ground-level passage and better hierarchy between base and upper volumes.
Choose the split direction to pull the form apart along the frontage-access relationship.
Introduce a sufficiently readable gap to register a public seam and strengthen section legibility.

Enlarge the carved void enough to read as usable public space rather than a shallow indentation.
Align the court opening to the verified access side so the ground response addresses the street edge.
Lower and clarify the terrace link so it becomes a legible public seam rather than a minor stepped interruption.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early massing object in all four views, so it clears simple coherence, but it under-delivers on the program’s required public threshold and active ground edge. The dominant form reads as a compact stepped block with some cantilever/terrace articulation, yet the stair-like tiering is more graphic than spatially necessary. The blue access edge is not met with a strong open seam, court, or undercut; instead the mass appears largely sealed and set back inconsistently from the frontage. The green parcel is respected, but the form mostly occupies it as a bounded object rather than organizing an occupiable void against the access side. Overall the geometry is legible, but the neighborhood-living brief wants a more public ground response and clearer void hierarchy than this candidate currently provides.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact low-rise composition with a central carved void and a bridge-like upper connector can support neighborhood/public program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is a single compact mass, not a multi-building complex; only the courtyard logic transfers.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like massing can organize multiple volumes around a shared courtyard/plaza while keeping a legible public center.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the open, spreading plan and reads more like a stepped object than an inhabited field.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A strong horizontal spread with a carved central void and a calm upper roof can ground mixed neighborhood uses.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more sectional and porous than the candidate; use it to deepen the void/terrace relationship.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/ribbon-like sectioning and connected wings can create sectionally meaningful public circulation and outdoor room.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate’s void is not yet as legible or as publicly useful as the reference’s courtyard-like center.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a void and void-under-block condition can maintain hierarchy while creating an active threshold.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the rendered views, but the access-side response is semantically weak.
The silhouette is coherent yet still reads as a stepped object more than a purpose-built neighborhood threshold.
One can see the mass in all views, so this is not a single-view illusion; the failure is programmatic and sectional, not basic visibility.
